newsitem.title: USA: JPM agrees to buy Denron for $23 mln.
newsitem.headline: JPM agrees to buy Denron for $23 mln.

text.p: The JPM Co said Monday it had signed a definitive agreement to merge with Denron Inc in a deal worth about $23 million.

The company said it will acquire all of Denron's stock in exchange for JPM common shares on a formula based on the average closing market valued for the 15 days prior to the closing of the transaction. The value of the deal cannot exceed $23 million, it added.
The two companies signed a letter of intent to merge in November.

Denron makes cable assemblies and wire harnesses with its main operations in San Jose, California and manufacturing support in China and Southeast Asia. Its sales for the fiscal year ended March 31, 1996 were $25 million.
JPM also makes cable assemblies and wire harnesses for original equipment manufacturers in the computer, networking and telecommunications sectors of the electronics industry.
